back: Non-metric, no hierarchy. E.g. gender, product category, region, purchase occasion.
Non-metric with a hierarchy. E.g. age groups, purchase frequency, emotions.
Metric, equal intervals but no true zero. E.g. IQ, Likert scales (satisfaction, NPS, brand attitude).
Metric, equal intervals and a true zero. E.g. age, income, revenues, sales.

Dichotomous → nominal
Rank order → ordinal
MC select one → nominal or ordinal
MC select many → nominal
Likert / semantic differential → metric interval
Customer Satisfaction Score = number of satisfied customers (4 and 5 on a 5-point scale) / number of responses × 100.
Net Promoter Score – measures loyalty: "How likely are you to recommend…?" (0–10). NPS = % promoters (9–10) − % detractors (0–6). Passives: 7–8.
Customer Effort Score: "The company made it easy for me to handle my issue" (1–7). CES = respondents with 5, 6, 7 / responses × 100.
Mean: average (metric data). Median: middle score after ordering (not for nominal). Mode: most frequent value – highest bar in a histogram (any variable).
Variance: average of the squared differences from the mean. SD: square root of the variance, same unit as the mean. Metric variables only.
Direction and strength of a LINEAR relationship between two metric variables; −1 ≤ r ≤ 1. r = 1 perfect positive, 0 no linear relationship, −1 perfect negative.
Descriptive: summarise characteristics of data. Causal: relationships and impact of a change in one variable on another. Exploratory: discover new connections.

front: LATCH – five ways to organise information

back: Size, orientation (hierarchies), shape, colour (categories), value, texture.

Bar: compare categories/change over time (≤10 bars). Pie: proportions (≤6–7 categories). Line: continuous data over time, trends. Area: part-to-whole volume. Scatter: correlation/clusters. Histogram: distribution. Gauge/bullet: KPI vs target, NPS. Radar: compare features.
